item.text: I’m checking what’s left that can be improved without turning this into churn. At this point the only useful refactor is reducing duplication around tree construction and making the API shape more coherent, so I’m verifying that before editing.

I found one real improvement worth making: the implementation still duplicates the whole encode pipeline for traversal order vs symbol order, and it never rejects negative frequencies. I’m folding those paths together behind an explicit order mode and tightening input validation.
The encode flow is consolidated now, and invalid data is rejected earlier. I’m updating the tests to cover the tighter contract before I re-run the whole set.
I’ve finished the edit pass. Next step is just compile-and-run verification to confirm the refactor didn’t move behavior on the legacy path and that the new validation tests pass.

Refactored [HuffmanCoding.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/033_huffman_coding/HuffmanCoding.java:7) to remove the duplicated encode pipeline. Both traversal-order and symbol-order outputs now go through a single `generateCodes(...)` path with an explicit `CodeOrder`, which makes the API behavior clearer and the implementation smaller. I also tightened validation so negative frequencies are rejected instead of being silently accepted.

I extended [HuffmanCodingTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/033_huffman_coding/HuffmanCodingTest.java:4) with null-frequency and negative-frequency coverage in addition to the existing behavior tests.
